title: Interval diagrams for enriched strings in a monoidal infinity category
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, full subcategories, cores and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Fix a monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ in a containing universe; no closure or colimits are assumed.

Let $\mathrm{RM}$ be the following ordinary category. Its objects are finite nondecreasing zero-one sequences of the forms $(0,1,\ldots,1)$ and $(1,\ldots,1)$, including the one-entry sequences $(0)$ and $(1)$. A morphism from $(i_0,\ldots,i_k)$ to $(j_0,\ldots,j_l)$ is a monotone map $a:[l]\to[k]$ with $j_t=i_{a(t)}$. The projection $\pi:\mathrm{RM}\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ remembers the ordinal. Write $q:\mathcal M=\mathrm{RM}\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal V^\otimes\to\mathrm{RM}$ for the degreewise pullback. The fiber at $(0,1)$ is $\mathcal V$ and the restriction to all-one sequences is $\mathcal V^\otimes$. An edge of $\mathcal M$ is called inert when its image in $\mathcal V^\otimes$ is inert.

Let $\mathrm{Po}$ be the full subcategory of the ordinary arrow category of $\Delta$ on consecutive-interval embeddings $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$. A morphism is a commutative square; let $\Theta$ remember its codomain and $\Phi$ its domain. Its fiber $\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}$ is the inclusion poset of nonempty intervals $[i,j]\subseteq[n]$. Define $\chi:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{RM}$ by $[n]\mapsto(0,1,\ldots,1)$ with $n+1$ ones and by $a\mapsto\mathrm{id}_{[0]}\star a$. There is a natural transformation $\bar\chi:\Delta^1\times\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{RM}$ from $\chi$ to the all-one sequence functor, obtained by dropping its first entry.

Define $\overline{\mathrm{Str}}(\mathcal V)\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ degreewise: an $r$-simplex over $u:\Delta^r\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a map $\Delta^r\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathrm{Po}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ over $\chi\Phi^{\mathrm{op}}$; here and below this fibre product is formed along $u$ and $\Theta^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathrm{Po}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, so over a vertex $[n]$ it is $\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Simplicial operators restrict these maps. Define $\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)$ as the full simplicial subset on interval diagrams $\sigma:\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ satisfying two conditions: inclusions with the same left endpoint are sent to inert edges, and, after a $q$-cocartesian lift of $\bar\chi$ dropping the first component, every interval-inclusion edge is inert in $\mathcal V^\otimes$. The second condition means that there exists such a lift with this property. Denote the projection by $p$. Restriction to singleton intervals remembers the tuple $(M_0,\ldots,M_n)$ and defines $r:\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)\to\Delta_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Here $\Delta_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the relative nerve of $F([n])=\mathcal V^{n+1}$, with tuple selection along monotone maps: an $r$-simplex consists of $u:[r]\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to F(u(\max J))$ for nonempty $J\subseteq[r]$, with $t_J|_{\Delta^I}=F(u(\max I)\to u(\max J))t_I$ for nonempty $I\subseteq J$; simplicial operators restrict these maps and apply their ordered vertex maps. Let $K=\mathcal V^\simeq$ be the core. Define $\mathrm{Str}_{\iota}(\mathcal V)$ by pullback along $\Delta_K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_{\mathcal V}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and denote its projection to $\Delta_K^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $r_\iota$. The relative nerve on a space is the model of [def-coef-complete-algebroid].

Define $\overline{\mathrm{Str}}^+(\mathcal V)\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the time-parametrized degreewise prescription: an $r$-simplex over $u:\Delta^r\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a simplicial map
$$\Delta^1\times(\Delta^r\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathrm{Po}^{\mathrm{op}})\longrightarrow\mathcal M$$
over $\bar\chi\circ(\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}\times\Phi^{\mathrm{op}})$, with the fibre product again along $u$ and $\Theta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its projection to $\mathrm{Po}^{\mathrm{op}}$ understood; simplicial operators restrict in the $\Delta^r$ parameter. Define $\mathrm{Str}^+(\mathcal V)$ as its full simplicial subset on objects $F:\Delta^1\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ such that $F_0:=F|_{\{0\}\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}}$ is an enriched interval string and the entire functor $F$ is a $q$-left Kan extension of $F_0$ along the full inclusion $\{0\}\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq\Delta^1\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Here the relative left Kan condition is specified using joins and relative colimit diagrams from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Regard the ordinary category $B_n=[1]\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and its full subcategory $A_n=\{0\}\times\mathrm{Po}_{[n]}^{\mathrm{op}}$ as their nerves. For every object $b\in B_n$, let $J_b$ be the nerve of the ordinary category of arrows $a\to b$ in $B_n$ with $a\in A_n$: a morphism from $a\to b$ to $a'\to b$ is an arrow $a\to a'$ in $A_n$ whose composite with $a'\to b$ is $a\to b$. Let $c_b:J_b^{\triangleright}\to N(B_n)$ be the canonical cocone, which sends such an arrow to its source $a$, sends the cone vertex to $b$, and uses the arrow $a\to b$ as its cocone edge. On a chain in $J_b$ its cone simplex is the corresponding chain of sources followed by $b$; repeated cone vertices give degenerate terminal arrows. The required condition is that
$$F\circ c_b:J_b^{\triangleright}\longrightarrow\mathcal M$$
is a $q$-colimit diagram for every $b\in B_n$, with its base diagram fixed to $qF c_b$. Thus the predicate uses all these cocones and their coherent simplices. This is the relative left Kan extension condition on $F$ itself. Let $a:\mathrm{Str}^+(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal V)$ be time-zero restriction. Evaluation at $(1,[n]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}[n])$ defines $e:\mathrm{Str}^+(\mathcal V)\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Call an edge of $\mathrm{Str}^+$ inert when its image under $a$ is $p$-cocartesian over an inert base arrow.
